GOT QUESTIONS?

Life Insurance FAQ

Clear answers about terms, underwriting, cash value, and beneficiary death benefits.

A common rule of thumb is 10 to 12 times your annual income. However, our advisors recommend adding outstanding mortgages, personal debts, and estimated future college tuition costs for your children, then subtracting existing liquid savings to find your precise coverage figure.
Term life covers you for a set period (such as 20 or 30 years) and pays out only if death occurs during that window; it is the most affordable type of life insurance. Whole life provides lifetime coverage with a guaranteed death benefit and builds cash value over time.
Yes! Surebound offers accelerated digital underwriting and simplified-issue life policies for qualified applicants up to age 60 and coverage limits up to $2,000,000 without requiring blood draws or physical examinations.
In the vast majority of cases, life insurance death benefits paid to named beneficiaries are completely free of federal and state income tax.
When your term concludes, you typically have three options: renew the policy on an annual basis, convert all or part of it into a permanent life policy without health questions, or let the coverage expire if your financial obligations have decreased.
